lines.text: An ER doesn't treat patients in the order they arrive.
A priority queue serves the highest priority first. The oldest item waits its turn. It's usually built on a heap. This is that heap, with a serving order.
Push low with five. Push urgent with one. Pop gives urgent. A heap puts the smallest number at the top. Schedulers, Dijkstra's algorithm, and notification systems rely on it.
Two items share priority one. The tie breaks by spelling. Low leaves before urgent.
Is priority-first always fair? Comment your take.
